name: Undersea cables & GPS
summary: Finnish court convicts Fitburg crew over Baltic cable damage; ruling appealable, no new cable cut found as of 8 Nov
state: A Helsinki court convicted the Fitburg's captain and boatswain of aggravated sabotage over cable damage on New Year's Eve, Yle reported on 5 Nov, finding the acts intentional; the ruling can be appealed. They received sentences of three and a half years and two years ten months (Euronews). Denmark's Bornholm station had logged 30 GPS jamming and spoofing incidents in 2026 by 10 Aug, against 16 in all of 2025 (European Pravda). Searches on 8 Nov found no new cable cut. The ruling concerns a past incident and is not final, so Watch holds.
for_you: Airlines and shipping in the Baltic are most exposed to satellite navigation interference. Internet users rarely notice a single cable fault because traffic reroutes.
rubric_hit: Watch: cable damage incident and GNSS interference affecting aviation. The 5 Nov sabotage conviction is about a past incident and is appealable; no new cuts isolating a region.

why: Subsea cables carry ~99% of intercontinental data; GPS jamming affects aviation and shipping.
drivers: Anchor drags, sabotage, conflict-zone jamming and spoofing.

rubric.alert: Multiple cable cuts isolating a region, or confirmed sabotage.
rubric.watch: Cable damage incident, or widespread GNSS interference affecting aviation.
rubric.normal: No new cable cuts or major jamming escalations.
